message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait/EFO and have acceptable endpoint labels (all are abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent AAA but still aligned). Two candidates (PGS003972/PGS003973; same Nat Genet AAA GWAS meta-analysis context) represent a disease-focused multi-cohort study family, which domain guidance says should usually outrank portability/framework-derived scores when endpoints are similarly faithful. Between those two, PGS003973 reports only a full-model C-index=0.882 (with basic age/age^2/sex covariates), which is not PRS-only and could be strongly covariate-driven; PGS003972 reports a lower full-model AUROC=0.69 but with broader multi-cohort development listed and multiple performance records (record_count=3), offering slightly more coherent validation support without relying on an outlier covariate-boosted metric. Competing models are mainly framework/portability-style (PGS001784 Cell Genom global biobank; PGS002054 UKB portability) or sparse older P+T (PGS000753). However, across all candidates, PRS-only AUROC is largely missing and reported PRS-only R2/partial-r are small (e.g., ~0.014–0.015), so the choice remains limited by non-comparable/missing PRS-comparable metrics, keeping confidence moderate and the overall outcome sub-optimal rather than high-quality."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait/EFO and have broadly aligned AAA diagnosis phenotypes (PGS000753 explicitly uses prevalent AAA; the others report AAA without obvious proxying). Several models come from pan-trait/framework or portability-style efforts (PGS001784: Global Biobank framework; PGS002054: UKB portability; PGS003429: cost-effectiveness/screening framing), which the provided domain policy says should generally not outrank a disease-focused direct-match model unless they have clearly stronger endpoint and PRS-comparable metric evidence. PGS000753 (MVP-focused AAA genetics paper) has the cleanest disease-focused context and reports a per-SD effect size (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates, supporting genuine PRS signal without relying on a full-model AUROC. However, the evidence is still limited/heterogeneous across candidates: PRS-comparable metrics are inconsistently reported, and the very high full-model discrimination in PGS003973 (C-index=0.882 with age/sex only) is not directly comparable to PRS-only performance and cannot be safely used as the primary separator under the stated rules. Because no single model has clearly superior, directly comparable PRS-only metrics across consistent validation settings, the selection is moderate-confidence and overall outcome is sub-optimal rather than high-quality."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait/EFO and have phenotype-aligned endpoints (mostly generic “abdominal aortic aneurysm”; one is “prevalent”). Several are from pan-trait/framework studies (PGS001784: Global Biobank framework; PGS002054: UKB portability framework), which domain guidance says to down-rank when disease-focused multi-cohort models exist. PGS003972/PGS003973 (Nat Genet AAA GWAS meta-analysis) appear disease-focused with broad multi-cohort development; among them, PGS003972 has a full-model AUROC=0.69 with unknown covariates and larger evidence package (record_count=3) than PGS003973 (single record; C-index=0.882 likely heavily driven by age/sex covariates and not PRS-comparable). Other options are weaker: PGS000753 is older, very sparse (29 variants), and uses a prevalent endpoint; PGS003429 is screening/cost-effectiveness framed with unknown covariates and lower AUROC (0.708). Overall, PGS003972 is preferred as the most clearly disease-focused, endpoint-faithful, multi-cohort score without relying on an apparently covariate-driven outlier metric; confidence is limited because key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/incremental AUROC) are missing or non-comparable across candidates and covariates are unknown for several top contenders."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait/EFO and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (AAA diagnosis; one is prevalent-only). Two candidates (PGS003972/PGS003973) come from a dedicated AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet 2023) with broad multi-cohort development, which domain guidance favors over pan-trait/framework/portability-derived scores when endpoints are similarly aligned. Between those two, PGS003972 is preferred because its reported evaluation uses an AUROC=0.69 without obvious heavy clinical covariate packaging (covariates listed as Unknown), whereas PGS003973 reports a high C-index=0.882 in a small validation (n=7,517) with explicit age/age^2/sex covariates—per the domain guidance, such high full-model discrimination can be largely covariate-driven and is not a PRS-only metric, making it less comparable as evidence of PRS contribution. Major limitation: across models, PRS-only AUROC is generally missing and several reported metrics are full-model or partial-r/R2 variants, so the evidence does not cleanly separate PRS contribution; thus confidence is not high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait/EFO and phenotyping_reported align to abdominal aortic aneurysm). However, the evidence is not cleanly comparable across models because most report only full-model AUROC/C-index (often covariate-influenced) or partial correlation, and several are from framework/portability studies (PGS001784: Global Biobank framework; PGS002054: UKB portability), which domain guidance says should be down-ranked when a disease-focused multi-cohort score exists. Among the disease-focused candidates, PGS003972/PGS003973 come from a dedicated AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet 2023) with broad multi-cohort development and EUR evaluation; PGS003972 reports a full-model AUROC=0.69 in EUR (n=6,940). PGS003973 reports a higher full-model C-index=0.882 but also includes age/age^2/sex covariates (basic but still makes the metric less PRS-comparable) and the metric type differs from AUROC, limiting cross-candidate interpretability. I therefore prefer PGS003972 as the more conservative disease-focused choice with a directly stated AUROC, while noting the main limitation: lack of clearly PRS-only metrics (AUROC/R2) for the disease-focused models prevents a high-confidence selection and keeps the outcome sub-optimal."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on concept/endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all align to abdominal aortic aneurysm, with PGS000753 specifically noting prevalent AAA). Several candidates come from pan-trait/portability frameworks (PGS001784: Global Biobank lessons; PGS002054: UKB portability), which domain guidance says should be down-ranked when a disease-focused multi-cohort alternative exists. PGS003972/PGS003973 (Nat Genet AAA GWAS meta-analysis) appear disease-focused with broad multi-cohort development and PRS-CS genome-wide construction, making them the strongest study-archetype fit among the set. Between these, PGS003973 reports a very high full-model C-index (0.882) but with only age/age^2/sex covariates; since PRS-only AUROC/R2 is not provided, that discrimination cannot be interpreted as PRS-comparable and could be largely covariate-driven. PGS003972 provides a more modest full-model AUROC (0.69) with similarly missing PRS-only metrics, but avoids the outlier-high full-model metric that is harder to attribute to the PRS contribution. Overall, PGS003972 is selected as the best-supported disease-focused direct-match, but confidence is limited because no candidate provides clearly comparable PRS-only discrimination across models, covariates are unknown for some, and performance evidence is heterogeneous/incomplete."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait/efo and phenotyping are abdominal aortic aneurysm, with one explicitly prevalent AAA). Two candidates (PGS002054 and PGS001784) are from framework/portability-style papers, and the domain policy advises down-ranking these when a disease-focused alternative exists unless they have clearly superior endpoint+PRS-comparable evidence. Among the disease-focused options, PGS000753 (MVP/Mayo-VDB Circulation AAA genetics paper) has clean basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), explicit per-SD effect size (OR=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44), and reasonable validation support (n=46,564); in contrast, the newer disease-focused Nat Genet family scores (PGS003972/PGS003973) report only full-model discrimination (AUROC/C-index) with missing PRS-only metrics and unclear/variable covariates, making cross-model PRS contribution hard to compare. Confidence is not high because several candidates lack PRS-only AUC/R2 and the strongest-looking full-model metric (PGS003973 C-index=0.882) cannot be treated as PRS-comparable per the provided policy, leaving limited comparable performance evidence to definitively separate disease-focused candidates."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait/EFO and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (AAA diagnosis/prevalent AAA), so selection hinges on study archetype and PRS-comparable evidence. PGS000753 (MVP Circulation AAA-focused study) provides the clearest PRS-specific signal via an effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and multi-cohort development (MAYO-VDB, MVP), aligning with the domain policy preference for disease-focused multi-cohort models over pan-trait/portability frameworks. Competing scores with explicit metrics are mostly framework-style: PGS001784 (global biobank lessons; PRS-only R2=0.0147 but full-model AUROC=0.868 is likely largely covariate-driven given extensive age/interaction terms), and PGS002054 (UKB portability; partial-r=0.0144). The newer disease-focused Nat Genet meta-analysis scores (PGS003972/PGS003973) report only full-model discrimination (AUROC=0.69; C-index=0.882) without PRS-only/incremental metrics, and covariates differ/are partly unknown, making cross-model comparability limited. Because most candidates lack directly comparable PRS-only AUROC/R2 and some reported discrimination appears full-model/covariate-influenced, the best choice is supported but not decisive, hence DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL with moderate confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait/efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (AAA diagnosis; one is prevalent).
